- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use lagged 3-day average as anchor.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the fall; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- Model consistently underestimates long-term (15+ day) price trends in bullish sentiment periods; increase forecast by 1–3% for horizon >10 days when sentiment >0.5.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.2–0.6), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows >10% deviation from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with that trend, especially if sentiment is trending upward.
